Extreem longtail: **4.745 combo's hebben 1 visit in 2 maanden**; ≥2 = 2.806 combo's / 11.471 visits, ≥5 = 710, ≥10 = 156. Gebouwd: de **2.806** van visits≥2, `status='built'`, 0 titels afgekapt op `MAX_TITLE_LEN=200` (langste 198), alle met `!!current_query!!` intact. Niets gepusht. Slechts 174 van 305k urls vielen af op parsing (67 zonder facet, 107 zonder resolvebare cat) — de slug→cat_id-map dekt dit vrijwel volledig.
- **De query is deterministisch:** exact dezelfde bytegrootte (40.918.591) als de ochtendrun van sessie `6d3ab396`. Handig als reproduceerbaarheidscheck.
- **Valkuil bij dubbele-prefix-checks:** een guard op `%beslist.nl/products/%beslist.nl%` geeft een false positive, want `utm_term=beslist.nl` / `utm_content=Beslist.nl%7C...` komen in echte urls voor (dezelfde reden waarom `q_newurls.sql` zijn `/c/`-`/p/`-`/r/`-predicaten op het **gestripte pad** uitvoert en niet op de ruwe url). Check op `startswith('https://www.beslist.nlhttps')`, niet op "komt beslist.nl twee keer voor".
- Deliverables: `Downloads\claude\SEO_titles_nieuwe_kandidaten_2026-07-27.xlsx` (6 tabbladen incl. drempelsets en de uitgesloten winkel-combo's). Scripts staan nog in `/tmp` scratchpad — zie BACKLOG.

## SEO-omzet loopt vanaf juli 2026 achter op vorig jaar — drie oorzaken, GEEN ervan SEO-specifiek (2026-07-27)

Analyse op vraag van Joep: SEO-omzet week 19–25 juli +7% WoW maar derde week op rij achter op vorig jaar. Geen code gewijzigd. YoY vergeleken met een **364-dagen shift** (52 weken) zodat zondag op zondag valt — kalenderdatums halen weekdagen door elkaar en dat vervuilt een zo–za-weekvergelijking. Excel: `Downloads\claude\SEO_deepestcat_wk19-25jul_vs_vorigjaar.xlsx`.

**Cijfers week 19–25 jul vs 20–26 jul 2025:** omzet_visit 77.984 → 54.924 (−29,6%), marge −24,1%, visits 608.194 → 488.715 (−19,6%), onze omzet (`click_revenue`) 68.482 → 53.578 (−21,8%). Drie weken op rij: −21,1% / −26,1% / −29,6%.

- **Oorzaak 1 — bol.com Plaza cliff op 10 maart 2026.** Clicks van ~20.000/dag naar ~7.000 in één dag (9 mrt 20.380 → 12 mrt 6.006), Amazon verdubbelde tegelijk. **Raakt ELK kanaal**, dus geen SEO-probleem: 18d voor/na → SEO −72%, SEA −78%, Overig Kanaal −70%, GSAAS −74%, AI −80%, maar **DMA paid slechts −31%** en DMA organic −31%. Die spreiding is nog onverklaard. Oorzaak zit in bol.com-feed/catalogus/commercieel; met SEO-werk niet te repareren.
- **Oorzaak 2 — CPR-billing switch 8 juli 2026** (`cpa_cpc` vast €0,12 → per-shop ROAS-pricing). Voor/na: visits/dag **−0,4%**, OPB **−14,7%**, omzet/dag −15,1%. Platform-breed. Vingerafdruk in de data = winnaars én verliezers met vlakke visits en wild uiteenlopende OPB (Rolgordijnen OPB 120 → 1.412; Vaatwassers 466 → 14, Dressoirs 737 → 89, Laptops 383 → 77 bij vrijwel stabiele visits).
- **Oorzaak 3 — wegvallen junihittegolf.** Seizoen, niet te fixen.

**Waarom "pas" 3 weken achter terwijl bol al in maart kantelde — basiseffect, geen nieuwe verslechtering.** De bol-drag was élke week aanwezig (−5.482 in week 19 apr → −10.331 in week 19 jul) maar werd volledig gemaskeerd. Gemiddeld per week: bol+amz drag apr–jun −7.888 → juli **−17.272**; rest-compensatie apr–jun +10.804 → juli **+3.166**. Samen ~−17k/week = precies de kanteling van +5,7% naar −21,1% YoY. Cruciaal: bol+amz deden **dit** jaar juist **+20%** (9.745 → 11.687/wk); de basis van **vorig** jaar sprong **+64%** (17.633 → 28.959/wk) door hun zomerpiek. De drag verergerde dus zonder dat er dit jaar iets veranderde. Amazon klapte daarbij van meewind (+2 à +3k/wk in het voorjaar, want begin 2025 was zwak) naar −6 à −7k/wk. **Augustus wordt zwaarder**: aug 2025 was de absolute piek (bol 86.064, Amazon 55.047 per maand, hoger dan juli).

**Marketplaces verklaren het gat meer dan volledig.** Top-4 −17.267 (bol NL −7.159 / Amazon Partners −4.847 / bol BE −3.173 / Amazon.nl −2.088) op een totaal gat van −14.904 → **de rest van het portfolio groeide +6,1%** (per dag zelfs +15% vs juli 2025). Bij bol/Amazon is het **100% volume**: −154.569 outclicks, terwijl de eCPC standhield of steeg (bol NL 0,1214 → 0,1333). Volume-effect −18.299 vs prijs-effect +1.032. GMV-impact (`revenue_excl`) −288.610. Aandeel bol+amz in SEO-omzet: 43–47% (jul–dec 2025) → 16,5–20,9% (2026).

**Dimensies van het gat:** 70% minder visits / 30% lagere OPB. **Hoe ondieper de pagina, hoe harder**: main_cat visits −27,1% vs sub_sub_cat −15,7%; hub-pagina's (deepest = maincat, 25% van de visits) −26,3% visits / −35,5% omzet vs diepere cats −17,5% / −27,8%. Type-url (native `dv.type_url`): PLP −44,2%, R-url −23,7%, C-url −24,1%, Homepage −62,4%. Device: **desktop −37,8% omzet vs mobiel −20,7%** — let op, er is **GEEN device-kolom op `dim_visit`**, gebruik `dv.viewport_group` (0-767 / 768-1023 / 1024+); echte device zit alleen in `bt.search_console` en `bt.websession_on_dataplatform` en die hebben geen bruikbare omzet. Breed geraakt: top-100 deepest cats = 78% van het gat, top-10 maar 25%.

- **Zomercats: twee verschillende vragen, niet verwarren — hier ging ik eerst de fout in.** Tegen **vorig jaar** zijn ze irrelevant (+485 op een gat van −23.067; visits-effect zelfs −226, hun plus is puur OPB en leunt op Jacuzzi's +379 wat repricing is). Maar tegen **week 21 juni** zijn ze **97% van de daling**: SEO 76.018 → 54.924 (−21.094), zomercats 25.250 → 4.782 (−20.468), overige 3.200 cats samen slechts −626. **Airconditionings alleen −10.980** (visits 33.978 → 2.090, −94%). Ik concludeerde eerst te breed "zomercats staan los van het probleem" op basis van alleen de YoY-test; Joep corrigeerde dat terecht. **Kalibratie:** week 21 juni was een uitschieter (zomercats normaal ≈6.580/wk) — tegen dat basisniveau is de daling ~−1.800, niet −20.468.
- **Naam-gebaseerde zomercat-indeling is ruw:** Jacuzzi's/Grasmaaiers zitten erin terwijl ze repricing resp. voorjaar zijn, en `Klimaatbeheersing` (−551) / `Luchtbehandeling` (−297) / hub `Huishoudelijk` (−2.374) vallen er juist buiten terwijl ze materieel airco zijn. Meegerekend komt het weerpakket op ruim −23.700, méér dan de totale weekdaling.

**Voorbehouden die bij elke YoY-omzetvraag horen:** `click_revenue`/`omzet_visit` settelen tot ~180 dagen na **conversiedatum**, dus recente weken staan structureel te laag tegenover volledig gesettelde weken van vorig jaar → elk recent YoY-gat is iets kleiner dan gemeten. Alles is **alle domeinen** (NL+BE+DE), consistent met de standup. Taxonomie-herstructurering vervuilde hier NIET: 99,9% van de visits zit in deepest cats die in beide jaren bestaan (74 cats alleen LJ = 162 visits, 96 alleen nu = 458) — wel altijd checken vóór een deepest-cat YoY.

**Redshift-gotchas onderweg:** `tag` én `delta` zijn reserved words; `dat.day_number` bestaat niet op `dim_date`; `information_schema.columns` met `ordinal_position <= N` → `cardinal_number_domain_check` (alles selecteren en client-side slicen); `marge`/`marketing_channel`/`bounce_clicks_visit` zitten op `bt.daily_standup_metrics_category` (met `deleted_ind=0`), NIET op `fct_visits` of `cpa_outclicks_transactional`; die laatste heeft `date` en géén `dim_date_key`, en géén `marge`/`device`; zo–za-weekbucket = `DATEADD(day,-1,DATE_TRUNC('week',DATEADD(day,1,<date>)))`.

## `bt.search_console` has synthetic placeholder keywords + mangles `?aff_id=` URLs — two traps for GSC analysis (2026-07-27)

Audited the GSAAS setup end-to-end (traffic, channel derivation, "feed" URLs). Nothing was broken in our code, but the investigation surfaced **two `bt.search_console` gotchas that will silently wreck any impression-level analysis**, plus two reasoning errors of mine worth recording as method lessons.

- **`keywords` contains SYNTHETIC PLACEHOLDER tokens — never treat an impression sum as real search demand without checking the keyword.** June 2026: `keywords='product'` spans **22,450 distinct URLs / 409,494 impressions / 1 click**; also `x` (81 urls / 21,821 impr) and `*` (16 urls). Real queries coexist alongside them in the same table (`ipad a16`, `ryzen 7 9800x3d` at avg_position 9-13), so a URL can look like a 300k-impression page when almost all of it is a placeholder bucket at ~0% CTR. Check the keyword distribution BEFORE quoting impressions or comparing CTR between URLs.
- **The ETL mangles URLs whose FIRST query param is `aff_id`.** It strips `?aff_id=<digits>` including the `?`, leaving the next `&` orphaned: `beslist.nl/?aff_id=734&utm_source=gsaas&…` is stored as **`beslist.nl/&utm_source=gsaas&…`**. Proof it's positional: the one June URL that KEPT its aff_id is `…/p/klussen/nl-nl-gold-5733439136242/?productId=4YGq…&aff_id=893` — there `aff_id` sits after `&`, so the pattern didn't match. A second stored variant carries un-decoded `&amp;` entities. `datamart.dim_visit` does the same aff_id stripping but **re-forms the `?` correctly**, which is why live visit URLs read `?utm_source=` while GSC reads `&utm_source=`. Consequence: GSC-keyed joins/reports on those URLs hang off a URL that does not exist (the correctly-formed `?utm` variant shows **7 impressions** for all of 2026). The job populating the table was never located — it is not in this repo.
- **Also remember `deleted_ind = 0`.** Without it the table hands you every soft-deleted version: `utm_source=gsaas` URLs are 323,909 rows unfiltered vs ~1,000–2,800 current rows per month.
- **Method lesson 1 — I called it "not an ETL artifact" on the wrong test.** I checked whether `&amp;`/`/&` were widespread table-wide; they weren't (1 URL each) and I read that as proof of a real site bug. Wrong: a *first-param*-stripping bug misfires on exactly one URL family, so a population of one is what the ETL explanation **predicts**, not evidence against it. Prevalence is not a valid test for a bug whose trigger is positional.
- **Method lesson 2 — I asserted SEO damage from impressions I hadn't validated** ("9x the homepage's impressions at 70x worse CTR" → brand cannibalization). Retracted: those were the `product` placeholder impressions above. And the root-cause guess ("someone typo'd the CSS Centre field") died the moment Joep pasted the screenshot — the config is correct. Ask for the config screenshot before theorising about which layer is broken.

## GSAAS channel — no Beslist-owned feed, ~92% CSS provider-link, and all-domain reporting is DELIBERATE (2026-07-27)

Durable facts about GSAAS (Beslist as a Comparison Shopping Service), from the same audit. No code changed.

- **Derivation:** `chan_deriv.ref_channel_derivation_stats` → **aff_id 734 + 750, channel_id 1**, both `deleted_ind=0`. **aff_id → domain is NOT 1:1**: aff 734 carries beslist.nl (domain 1) **and shopcaddy.de (domain 12)**; aff 750 = beslist.be (domain 2). Long-standing (≥ Jan 2025), not a regression. Likely cause: CSS Centre account **140784594** hardcodes `aff_id=734` in its link fields, so any domain configured the same way lands in the NL affiliate.
- **GSAAS uses NO product feed of ours.** ~92% of visits carry `utm_content=css-provider-link` — the mandatory "By Beslist.nl" attribution badge, whose destinations are configured **once per CSS account** in CSS Centre ("Links to your business"), not per-product: Homepage URL `https://www.beslist.nl/?aff_id=734&utm_source=gsaas&utm_medium=paid-search&utm_campaign=css&utm_content=css-provider-link` and Product search URL `https://www.beslist.nl/products/r/$0/?aff_id=734&…`. **`$0` = Google substituting the user's raw search query**, which is what generates the `/products/r/<query>/` landings. Product-page landings are negligible (~28 `/p/` visits per week), so don't look for feed `link` attributes in this channel — those live in the Direct Shopping / DMA accounts.
- **The `$0` passthrough is unfiltered**, so foreign-language and non-commercial queries hit NL/BE search pages: Turkish `parfümler erkek` / `puma iş ayakkabısı`, Polish `Jedwabna poszewka na poduszkę 50x60` on **beslist.be**, German `was tun um herz zu stärken`. Percent-encoding is valid UTF-8 (`%C4%B1` = Turkish dotless ı) — **not** a mojibake bug, genuine user input. Consistent with ~77% bounce on the search-page bucket (bare-homepage bucket ~92%). Jul 1–26 2026: 46,950 visits → ~€3,150.
- **`seo_stats_service.py` (3 fct_visits queries) and `performance_standup_service.py` (4) deliberately DO NOT filter `dv.domain`** — so both report **NL+BE+DE combined**. Joep was asked on 2026-07-27 and chose to leave it. Reason: the standup Excel's whole history (~2,800 rows since 2025, plus a `YOY` sheet) was written by this code and is all-domain — verified day-for-day against the unfiltered query (2026-06-29 = 2072, 06-30 = 1878, 07-01 = 1933, exact). Switching would step-change the series mid-stream. **Do not "fix" this.** NL-only impact if ever wanted (Jul 1–26): SEO −18.1%, DMA organic −15.7%, GSAAS −10.2%. Note this intentionally differs from the canonical bot-filtered real-visits pattern, which pins `domain='1'`.
- **Diagnosing a GSAAS volume move: compare against Google Shopping, not SEO.** The late-July 2026 dip (−23% w/w on aff 734) was uniform across every landing bucket and matched Google Shopping (−19.1% 14d/14d) while SEO held at −3.8% and DMA paid was flat → Google-side/seasonal, not a config break. YoY Jul is structurally softer too: NL −15%, BE −29%, DE +32%.
- Redshift gotchas hit on the way: `tag` is a **reserved word**; `dat.day_number` doesn't exist on `dim_date`; `information_schema.columns` with `ordinal_position <= N` throws `cardinal_number_domain_check` (select all and slice client-side); `bounce_clicks_visit` is on `daily_standup_metrics_category`, NOT `fct_visits` (there, derive bounce from `number_of_{cpc,ww}_productclicks = 0`). Full-table `url LIKE` scans on `bt.search_console` routinely exceed 120s — run them backgrounded.

## DMA Exclusions Timestamp showed UTC as if local — the shared Postgres is `Etc/UTC` (2026-07-27)

Joep spotted `2026-07-27 07:43` on item `nl-nl-gold-8720526007155` for a run he remembered doing ~09:45. He was right; the stored value was also right. Fixed in **`ef5c53e`** (`frontend/dma-exclusions.html`, display-only).

- **The shared Postgres at `10.1.32.9` runs `TimeZone = Etc/UTC`.** So `now()` into a `TIMESTAMP` (no tz) column stores the **UTC** wall-clock, not Amsterdam. Verified: `now()` = 10:22 UTC while Amsterdam was 12:22. Offset +2 CEST / +1 CET. `dma_exclusions.created_at/applied_at` are exactly this shape (`TIMESTAMP DEFAULT now()`), so the record's true local time was 09:43:21 — matching Joep's recollection to within two minutes.
- **Nothing converted anywhere in the chain:** server UTC → naive `TIMESTAMP` → backend `.isoformat()` emits **no offset** (`dma_exclusions_service.py:1264`) → the cell did pure string work on that ISO text, `esc(x.applied_at).replace("T"," ").slice(0,16)`. UTC digits presented as local.
- **The trap in fixing it:** `new Date(s)` on an offset-less date-time parses as **LOCAL** per spec, so the obvious fix is a no-op in CEST and would shift the value again for a viewer in another zone. New `fmtTs()` appends an explicit `"Z"` first, then formats with `toLocaleString("sv-SE", { timeZone: "Europe/Amsterdam", … })` — sv-SE yields `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`, preserving the shape the column always had, and DST comes free (07:43Z → 09:43 in July, 08:43 in January). Unparseable input falls back to the old slice rather than rendering "Invalid Date".
- **Display-only by design:** stored values stay UTC and `savedSortVal` still sorts the **raw** ISO field, so sorting is unaffected. The cell keeps the raw value on a `title` tooltip and the column header now names the timezone. That slicing pattern occurred **only** at that one line across all frontend html — checked before assuming it was systemic. Static file → browser refresh, no uvicorn restart.

## GSD LL mystery run resolved — two independent sources, tripwire nailed it (2026-07-22)

The "mysterious automatic GSD low-linkage Pause/Enable runs" turned out to be **two unrelated things** wearing one costume. The tripwire logging (`3bf8995`, 21 Jul: WARNING on `/ll/run`+`/ll/apply` with IP/UA/call-stack, plus `run_low_linkage STARTED` with port/pid) is what let us split them. Investigation ran on the prod box by l.davidowski's Claude; transcript at `C:\Users\JoepvanSchagen\Downloads\claude\gsd_ll_onderzoek_2026-07-22.txt`. DB audit counts (`pa.jvs_gsd_ll_campaigns`) and prod `service.log` agreed exactly (121 mutations = 50 paused / 71 enabled) → cross-validated.

- **Source 1 — the genuinely automatic 09:50 CEST run. CLOSED.** Pre-fix scheduler called `run_low_linkage(dry_run=False)` **directly** (no HTTP, no IP), running inside **zombie uvicorn instances on ports 8003/8098/8099** serving OLD code. Produced the 18–21 Jul 09:50 batches. Fixed by killing the zombies + changing `_excel_scheduled_run` to load-only. **22 Jul 09:50 was clean** (Excel load only). Lesson: multiple/zombie uvicorn instances each run their OWN in-process APScheduler — a code fix only takes effect on instances that are actually restarted onto the new code; leftover instances keep executing the old behavior. Enforce a single prod instance + disable vestigial launchers (see `dm_tools_backend_no_reload`).
- **Source 2 — a HUMAN via the dashboard. STILL POSSIBLE.** Today's noon "run" was manual: `/ll/run?dry_run=true&source=excel` @ 11:50 → 6 min polling → `/ll/apply` (121 entries) @ 11:58 → done 12:00. Classic preview→wait→Apply. Not automatic. Came from IP `94.142.210.226` (Chrome 150 / Win) — the **only** IP that ever hits these endpoints, active since ≥10 Jul (277 real mutations that day).
- **Correction to the 21 Jul theory:** the 09:50 automatic runs were NOT HTTP calls from `94.142.210.226` — that IP is a **human browser** (almost certainly the Beslist office/VPN NAT egress → identifies the network, not a person). The two were conflated because both peaked around midday on 17 Jul (both sources fired that day).
- **Prod facts:** uvicorn `--port 3003` on `win-htz-006.colo.beslist.net` (HTTPS), log `C:\Users\l.davidowski\dm-dashboard\logs\service.log` (~1.9 GB); dashboard `https://win-htz-006.colo.beslist.net:3003/static/gsd-campaigns.html`. `_get_server_port()` reads `--port` from `sys.argv`; the 3003-only Slack guard + notifications key off it.
- **Open / follow-up:** who clicked Apply @ 11:58 (shared IP → ask around); **`/ll/run`+`/ll/apply` have no auth** → backlogged (BACKLOG.md → "GSD Campaigns (Low-Linkage)"); interim guard = kill switch (was OFF on prod). Full write-up: `GSD_LL_MYSTERY_RUN.md`.

## SEO Titles — `pa.page_titles_existing` has TWO merged column layouts; the tool's two config APIs (2026-07-21)

Built out the SEO Titles "Built titles" panel + inline editing (commits `236a0d5`, `a9f2a8d`, `6fdd6d1` on main; deployed :8003). Durable findings:

- **`pa.page_titles_existing` (the tblPageTitles export) contains TWO row layouts merged from different export generations — a single fixed column mapping is wrong for ~71% of rows:**
  - *normal* (~28%, `title` contains `beslist.nl`): `key`=facet combo, `title`=page title, `h1_title`=H1, `description`=meta description.
  - *shifted* (~71%, capitalized `key` e.g. "Games"): `key`=**category name**, `title`=**facet combo**, `h1_title`=**page title**, `description`=**H1** (there is NO meta description in this layout).
  Discriminator that works: `title ILIKE '%beslist.nl%'` → normal, else shifted. `get_preview(status='existing')` normalises both into (facet key / title / h1 / description). Because shifted rows carry no meta and neither layout reliably stores a category name, two columns are backfilled **by `cat_id` (reliable in both layouts)**: `cat_name` from the taxonomy CSV cache (`scripts/backfill_page_titles_existing_catname.py`, 98.5%) and `browse_description` from the website-config API (below, 98.3%). `load_pagetitles_existing.py` TRUNCATE+reloads, so **both backfills must be re-run after a reload** (its DDL now declares the columns + prints a reminder).

- **website-configuration `/html-title-descriptions` API** (same host + `X-Api-Key`=`UNIQUE_TITLES_API_KEY` as `/page-titles`): `GET /html-title-descriptions/{cat_id}` → array of ONE **category-level** record `{cat_id, country_code, browse_with_query_title, browse_empty_title, browse_description, details_title, details_description, h1_title, last_update}`. Per-category, not per-facet-combo. GET without an id → 405. Used `browse_description` to fill Existing-combo meta descriptions.

- **The Taxonomy API has NO description field** — a category payload is only `{id, parentId, is*flags, labels{name,urlSlug}, subCategories, facets}`. Don't look there for page meta descriptions (the original request assumed taxonomy; it was the website-config API).

- **Generator `facet_phrase` (seo_titles_service):** `geschikte_leeftijd` rendered before the category noun (its `order_index`=972 < the sub_category slot 1700). Fixed by pinning it to `noun_order + 0.5` (noun = max type-facet order, or 1700 when none) so it always renders AFTER the category/type-facet. Type-facet `order_index` ranges 3→1854, so no single fixed number works — hence the computed offset. Regenerated the 1,041 existing built rows via `build_blueprint`.

- New endpoints `POST /api/seo-titles/update` (edit a built/pushed/failed blueprint in place) and `/create-built` (edit an Existing combo → new `status='built'` blueprint, which "moves" it into the Built set). Edit UI is a hand-rolled centered overlay (dimmed backdrop, only Save/Cancel close it) — no Bootstrap modal dependency. UI_BLUEPRINT.md gained: fixed-vs-content-width table strategies + no-bleed rule, filter-row + sort-arrow layout, right-pinned sticky action column for hover controls.

## FAQ export JSON 500'd on a raw control character (strict `json.loads`) (2026-07-21)

`GET /api/faq/export/json` (`backend/main.py`) 500'd with "Invalid control character at: line 1 column 96 (char 95)". One row of 269,793 (`schema_org`, url_id 3110993) had a literal newline inside a stored JSON string; strict `json.loads` rejects control chars in strings. The XLSX export already stripped them via regex, which is why only the JSON export failed. Fix: `json.loads(x, strict=False)` for both `faq_json` and `schema_org` — accepts the char on read, `json.dumps` re-escapes it to valid `\n` on write. Commit `236a0d5`. (Aside: that endpoint buffers the entire ~1.9 GB response in memory before streaming — a separate scalability smell, not fixed.)

## Auto-Redirects — a "cross-subcat" redirect traced to a stale `facets.csv`; added a Refresh-facets button + auto-refresh-before-run (2026-07-21)

User flagged a redirect that "crossed to another category": `.../meubilair_389370_389409/r/riviera_maison/` → `.../meubilair_389369_10538533/c/merk~4874240` (score 90, tier A, reason `[maincat] Matched 1 facet 'Riviera Maison'`). Same maincat (meubilair), different **subcat**. User then pointed out the correct same-subcat target `.../meubilair_389370_389409/c/merk~4874240` **is live**. Root cause was NOT matcher logic — it was the **facet snapshot**.

- **`facets.csv` is the engine's whole world for pass-1 matching, and it's a cached Search-API snapshot.** `main_parallel_v2.py` pass 1 (`filter_by_subcategory(subcat_id)`, ~line 1521) matches only against rows in `rurl_optimizer_v2/data/cache/facets.csv`. That CSV is built by `db_loader.py::load_facets` firing **one bare Search-API call per subcategory** and recording only `(cat, facet, value)` combos the API *returned* ("only combos that actually have products, as reported by the Search API"). **Verified the gap directly:** the cache had **0 rows for category_id 389409** (the whole subcat was absent — Search API returned nothing for its slug at build time) and Riviera Maison (value `4874240`) appeared **exactly once**, under subcat `10538533` (count=1). So pass-1 had an empty candidate set → fell through to the maincat-wide rescue (`filter_by_main_category`) → found Riviera Maison only under `10538533` → routed there, tagged `[maincat]`. The live same-subcat `/c/merk~4874240` was never visible to the optimizer. This is the same Search-API flakiness noted elsewhere (bare category calls silently drop facets/whole cats non-deterministically; combo facets need a filter to surface). The runtime `facet_probe.py` live-probe layer supplements the snapshot for the Fix-D/enrichment paths but **not** pass-1 subcat matching.
- **`facets.csv` is never rebuilt on a schedule — build-once, then reused forever.** `load_facets` returns the cached CSV whenever the file exists; every production run passes `use_cache=True` (`preload_data`). The only rebuild triggers were: delete the file, or manually run `python -m src.db_loader` (its `__main__` forces `use_cache=False`). The live copy was dated **Apr 28** — ~**84 days** stale at the time (status endpoint reported `age_days: 84.26`).
- **Rebuild cost ≈ 5–8 min, network-bound.** ~3,540 subcategories (`categories.csv` rows), `MAX_WORKERS=12`, measured live Search-API latency ~870 ms/call (280 ms deep subcat → 1.6 s big maincat) → ~4–5 min for the facet fetch + ~1–3 min for the upfront taxonomy tree crawl. That cost is exactly why it's cached.
- **Shipped (commits `c535587` feature, `0706237` colour fix; deployed via kill+relaunch :8003):** a **Refresh facets** button on the Auto-Redirects tool (left of Run) that rebuilds `facets.csv` in the background; new endpoints `POST /api/rurl-v2/refresh-facets` + `GET /api/rurl-v2/refresh-facets/status` backed by a lock-guarded rebuild (`DataLoader(use_cache=False).load_facets()` in a subprocess mirroring the run's cwd/env). A successful rebuild **drops the shared preload pickle** `/tmp/r_url_optimizer_cache.pkl` so the next run picks up the fresh snapshot (the pickle is derived from `facets.csv` and would otherwise pin the stale data). **`start_optimize` now auto-refreshes before a run when the cache is > `FACETS_MAX_AGE_DAYS` (7)** — runs inside the background worker thread, logs progress into the run, and on refresh failure logs a warning and continues with the existing cache rather than aborting the user's run.

## GSD LL "last successful data load" reset on every restart — mtime + DB persistence (2026-07-21)

The LL card's purple-"i" tooltip ("Last successful data load: …") changed on every backend restart. Root cause in `gsd_ll_service.py::load_excel_data`: `loaded_at = datetime.now()` written ONLY to the in-process `_EXCEL_DATA` cache. Each restart runs a startup pre-load → re-stamps the current time → the tooltip showed the last **restart**, not the last real ~09:50 data load. (A 2026-07-17 fix `90796f9` to use file mtime had regressed back to `now()` — same kind of silent revert as the GSD history column-width regression found the same day; watch for these.)

- **Fix part 1 — date from the Excel file's mtime, not the clock.** `loaded_at = datetime.fromtimestamp(os.path.getmtime(path), AMSTERDAM_TZ).isoformat()`. The scheduled script writes a fresh `gsd_shops_nl_be_*.xlsx` ~09:50 daily; its mtime is the true data date and is stable — re-reading the same file across restarts yields the same value. Falls back to `now()` only on `OSError`.
- **Fix part 2 — persist to a singleton DB table** `pa.jvs_gsd_ll_excel_load` (n8n-vector-db, `id INTEGER PK DEFAULT 1 CHECK (id=1)`, upsert `ON CONFLICT (id)`). `_record_excel_load()` after each successful load (best-effort, never raises); `get_last_excel_load()` reads it (converts the TIMESTAMPTZ back to an ISO string to match the in-memory shape). `get_excel_data_status()` falls back to the persisted row when in-memory `loaded_at` is None — so the date is retrievable across restarts AND across the two instances (this box + win-htz-006). DB read happens only when the in-memory value is absent (no per-request overhead on the prod box after its pre-load).
- **Frontend** (`gsd-campaigns.html`): the tooltip now uses `d.loaded_at` regardless of `has_data` (the persisted value is the last real load even when the feed isn't cached in this process). TZ display is consistent: in-mem returns `+02:00`, DB returns `+00:00`, both the same instant → `new Date(iso).toLocaleString('nl-NL')` renders 09:50 either way.
- **Dev-box caveat:** on this WSL box the Excel path (`C:\Users\l.davidowski\…`) is unreachable, so `loaded_at` stays null here (same reason startup logs show the "no xlsx found" retries); it populates on the box that can read the file. Commit `248877d`, deployed (kill+relaunch :8003). Test rows truncated → table empty, ready for first real load.

## Local folder consolidation: `dm-tools` renamed to `dm-dashboard`, single working copy (2026-07-21)

This box had TWO local checkouts of the same GitHub repo (`joep-1993/dm-dashboard`): `projects/dm-tools` (served live :8003, up-to-date) and a stale `projects/dm-dashboard` (7 behind, occasionally edited). Merged into ONE folder named `dm-dashboard`. The old `joep-1993/dm-tools` GitHub repo was already archived (remote alias `archived-dm-tools`); the repo-level split was gone, only the local-folder duplication + confusing naming remained.

- **ALWAYS check the "stale" folder is idle before `rm -rf`.** The `dm-dashboard` folder that looked stale had **uncommitted cc1 edits written minutes earlier** (`find -mmin -5`, freshly-modified LEARNINGS/TASKS) — a concurrent session was mid-task in it. Deleting would have destroyed real work. Preserved it: extracted the additive cc1 blocks and committed them on main (`cc82397`) BEFORE deleting. Pre-flight checks that caught it: `find <dir> -type f -mmin -30`, `ls -l /proc/*/cwd | grep <dir>`, `git rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...origin/main`, `git status`.
- **Relocate the venv in place (sed the shebangs) — do NOT recreate from requirements.txt.** `requirements.txt` pinned only 22 of the 79 installed packages (the rest are transitive/hand-installed) → a recreate would silently lose deps. The old path appeared only in ~23 text scripts under `venv/bin/*` + `pyvenv.cfg`: `grep -rlI 'projects/dm-tools' venv/ | xargs sed -i 's|projects/dm-tools|projects/dm-dashboard|g'`. `venv/bin/python*` are symlinks to `/usr/bin/python3` (unaffected). Captured `pip freeze` first as a safety net. Verified `venv/bin/python -c "from backend.main import app"` (301 routes) after.
- **`.env` does NOT travel in git — reconcile it explicitly.** The stale folder's `.env` was 9 lines shorter, missing 4 live keys (`GSD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE` pinned SA path, `ENABLE_TASK_SCHEDULER`, `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`, `SLACK_USER_ID`) and had one the live one lacked (`GSD_SHEETS_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE`, which IS used by `gsd_campaigns_service.py`/`gsd_budgets_service.py` — works today only via a code default). Used the LIVE folder's `.env` as source of truth; rewrote the absolute `GSD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE` path to the new folder; added `GSD_SHEETS_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE`; kept `DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` empty (= no dashboard auth, per user).
- **THREE launchers existed; only ONE actually boots the server.** The real boot launcher is **Windows Task Scheduler task `\DM Tools Dashboard` (trigger: At logon) → `C:\Users\JoepvanSchagen\scripts\start-dm-dashboard.ps1`** (confirmed: last-run 09:10 today, result 0 = the process live when the session started). The other two were vestigial and would have masked the real one: the Startup-folder `start-dm-dashboard.vbs` **also** launched uvicorn at logon (double-launch; the 2nd just failed to bind :8003) — **deleted it**; and the repo `start-dm-tools.bat` claims TS "at startup" but **no task references it** — dead. Find the real one via `schtasks.exe /query /fo CSV /v` (grep the "Task To Run" column) or grep `/mnt/c/Windows/System32/Tasks/`. The `.ps1` hardcoded `/projects/dm-tools` on 2 lines → would have **broken the next logon boot**; fixed. Also **dropped `--reload`** from the `.ps1` to match the documented bare-uvicorn live behavior ([[dm_tools_backend_no_reload]]).
- **~30 hardcoded `/home/joepvanschagen/projects/dm-tools` absolute paths** in standalone scripts (`scripts/analysis/*`, prototypes, koptekst*), `backend/add_visits_revenue.py`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `notes/*.txt` — fixed with a scoped sed (commit `caebbed`). Left as-is: comment/docstring product-name mentions ("dm-tools style/venv"), UI footer/labels (the app IS branded "DM Tools"), the Google-Ads label description string in `campaign_processor.py`, and the historical migration doc.
- **`cc1/` is `.gitignore`d but its files are force-tracked** → `git add cc1/X` prints "paths are ignored … exits 1", which **silently breaks `git add … && git commit …` chains** (commit never runs) even though the file DID stage. Use **`git add -f cc1/...`**. (Bit me twice this session; the files staged anyway so the commits still landed, but use `-f` to be safe.)
- **Drift risk is NOT eliminated** — only the local duplicate-folder confusion was. The other Claude on the networked box `win-htz-006.colo.beslist.net:3003` still has its OWN checkout pushing to the same GitHub repo → keep the fetch-before-push / reconcile discipline. ## Healthscore 2.0 — seasonal caps go all-channel + one-month look-ahead; committed & deployed (2026-07-21)

Resumed HS2.0 (parked since 2026-07-20). It was fully built (Phases 1–6 + 3.5 seasonal caps), validated, but **uncommitted**. This session: two cap-model changes, a comparison deliverable, and the first commit.

- **Seasonal cap now sized on ALL-CHANNEL visits, not SEO-only** (user preference). Added `_ALL_JOIN`/`_ALL_WHERE` (drop the `marketing_channel='SEO'` predicate + the chan_deriv join, keep `is_real_visit=1` + beslist.nl URL filter). Both cap sources — `_refresh_cat_month` (24mo climatology) and `_refresh_cat_knee` (12mo coverage-knee) — use them. **The coverage KPI and the URL score stay SEO-only** — only the cap *sizing* signal is all-channel. Rebuild grew the universe 3,574→3,608 cats (all-channel picks up cats with no SEO but other-channel visits).
- **One-month forward-max look-ahead** on the seasonality multiplier: `mult(m) = max(index[m], index[m+1])` (Dec wraps to Jan), applied before alpha/clamp; the stored `season_index` column now records the effective (forward-max) value. Rationale: SEO needs lead time, so a cap should ramp up *before* the demand peak. Forward-max (vs a pure +1 shift) ramps early AND holds the peak month high — a pure shift would *drop* the cap during the actual peak (it'd use the post-peak month's lower index). Verified on Airco: all-channel peak is May–Jun (idx 5.5) and May got pulled up to June's level.
- **The `pa.hs2_cat_cap.yearly` column is total trailing-12mo visits per cat (MAX(tot) in the knee SQL), NOT a year label** — that's why its range is 1→591,675 (smallest→largest cat). Provenance only; not used in selection.
- **June holdout CANNOT exercise the look-ahead.** Forward-max only lifts *run-up* months; it never changes a month already at/after its peak. In June the seasonal test cats (Airco, Grasmaaiers) are all at/past peak, so their June cap is unchanged (+0.0). To measure the look-ahead's payoff you must backtest a run-up month (e.g. May for Airco). On the June 10-cat set the changes gave only +0.7pp vis / +0.2pp rev vs the SEO-only/no-look-ahead caps — and that delta is entirely the bigger all-channel knee, at +13% footprint (20.2k→22.9k URLs on the sample).
- **URL-type mix is the whole HS2.0 thesis in one view** (10-cat set, via `dim_visit.type_url` w/ URL-pattern fallback for the ~30% NULLs): HS2.0 vs HS1.0 → **R-url 2.6%→22.6%** (the uncovered-SEO lever), **PLP 53.9%→28.9%** (product-page padding halved), C-url 43.4%→48.5%, Cat-url (bare `/products/cat/id`, no `/c/` `/r/`) ~0.1% both. `type_url` values seen: `C-url`, `PLP`, `R-url`, `Browse-url zonder /r/ en /c/`, `Homepage`, NULL. **PLP == PDP `/p/` in Beslist parlance** (merge them). `type_url` is ~30% NULL (incl. all `/p/` product pages) so pattern-fallback is required for a complete split.
- **Deploy state:** the live :8003 (pid started 09:08 today) already served the on-disk HS2.0 code — `/api/healthscore/health` = 200 (open, not behind the earlier auth challenge). **Committed** the full HS2.0 (Phases 1–6 + 3.5) as `e423557` on main (45 files, feat(healthscore)), pushed to dm-dashboard. cc1 docs excluded from that commit (this ucp handles them). Deliverables in `Downloads/claude/`: `HS2.0_vs_HS1.0_vergelijking.xlsx` (5 sheets) + `hs2_catdiff_seasonal_v2.csv`; builder `scripts/analysis/healthscore_catdiff_excel.py`. **Next: implement HS2.0 for the 10 test categories.**

## Unique-title mojibake — root cause was `cat_urls.csv` content itself + the doubled-word brand minefield (2026-07-21)

User reported garbled H1s in the Unique-title DB (`pa.unique_titles_content`): `ImprimÃ©tops` (should be `Imprimétops`), `plissã©gordijnen` (should be `plisségordijnen`). Classic UTF-8-decoded-as-Latin-1 mojibake (`é`=C3A9 → `Ã©`; a downstream `.lower()` turned `Ã©` → the lowercased `ã©` variant).

- **DB repair (done, reversible).** Two passes on `pa.unique_titles_content` (cols h1_title/title/description/original_h1). (1) **Mojibake: 1,100 rows** — repaired with a map over cp 0xA0–0xFF that adds BOTH the uppercase form (`Ã©`) and the lowercased-first form (`ã©`); regex-replace (NOT whole-string `.encode('latin-1').decode('utf-8')` — the strings contain `✔️` which isn't latin-1-encodable). Backup `pa.unique_titles_content_bak_mojibake_20260721`. (2) **Doubled words: 5,312 rows** — the corruption also produced adjacent duplicate words (`föhns föhns`, `jaloezieën jaloezieã«n`) because the generator saw the clean vs mojibaked forms as two tokens. Backup `pa.unique_titles_content_bak_dupword_20260721`.
- **The doubled-word DEDUP is a brand minefield — never blindly collapse `\b(\w+)\s+\1\b`.** Of 319 distinct duplicated tokens, many are **legitimate doubled-name brands**: Joseph Joseph, Miu Miu, Samsøe Samsøe, Noa Noa, Tuc Tuc, Pom Pom, Uoga Uoga, Holika Holika, Naf Naf, Cache Cache, Anaïs Anaïs, Balm Balm, VTech Zoef Zoef / Toet Toet — plus numeric coincidences (`Galaxy Watch 5 5 ATM` = model + water-resistance, not a dup). Applied a "safe-broad" rule: collapse EXCEPT a brand whitelist + numeric tokens + single letters. ~681 adjacent-dups intentionally left (protected). Always audit the collapsed-token frequency before writing.
- **ROOT CAUSE = the source data file, not a live decode bug.** The live path (`ai_titles_service.generate_title_v3`/`generate_title_from_api` → `faq_service.fetch_products_api` → h1) reads the productsearch API with `response.json()` (clean UTF-8) and gets the **category name from `backend/data/cat_urls.csv`** via `category_lookup.lookup_category`. That CSV is valid UTF-8-with-BOM but its **content was already mojibaked** — 27/3558 rows literally stored `PlissÃ©gordijnen`, `FÃ¶hns`, `ImprimÃ©tops`, `JaloezieÃ«n`, `SleeÃ«n`. So the pipeline read it *correctly* and faithfully propagated the corruption into every generated title. Reproduced live: `fetch_products_api(...)['category_name']` returned `'PlissÃ©gordijnen'` before the fix.
- **The bug CLASS is `requests`' ISO-8859-1 fallback** — how the CSV got corrupted upstream (whatever scraped the category names had it) and a still-live risk in the kopteksten scraper. When Beslist serves `text/html` with **no `charset`** in the Content-Type header (which it does for our scraper UA `"Beslist script voor SEO"` — verified: `charset-in-header: False`, `requests .encoding: ISO-8859-1`), `response.text` decodes UTF-8 as Latin-1. Already documented + fixed in `seo_rulings_service.py:289` but was **missing** elsewhere. NB the normal-UA request DOES get `charset=UTF-8` — the no-charset behaviour is UA-specific.
- **Fixes shipped (commit `bc68056`, deployed).** (1) New `backend/text_encoding.py::fix_mojibake` — the validated repair map; **no-op on clean text** (zero false positives across ~1M title rows; leaves `Joseph Joseph`/`Nike Air Max` intact). (2) Wired into `category_lookup._load()` (repair maincat/deepest_cat on read) and `fetch_products_api` (repair assembled h1/category on output) — so corruption can't propagate even if the CSV/API regress. (3) Repaired the 27 rows in `cat_urls.csv` on disk (BOM/CRLF/`;` preserved; backup `cat_urls.csv.bak_mojibake_20260721`). (4) Added `response.encoding = "utf-8"` before `.text` in `scraper_service.py` (live kopteksten path, UA has same no-charset issue) and the **dead** `scrape_page_h1` (ai_titles_service.py — defined once, **zero callers**, was a red herring). `main.py:3965/4129` use `httpx` (defaults utf-8, low risk) — left alone.
- **Investigation technique that localized it fast:** confirm the DB is clean end-to-end (`SHOW client_encoding/server_encoding` = UTF8; psycopg2 default utf-8) → test each source (MySQL `nl-nl_FacetValue` returns clean under `utf8mb4` AND default; JSON APIs send `charset=utf-8`) → reproduce with the exact scraper UA → then `file cat_urls.csv` (UTF-8 w/ BOM) + `grep -a` the accented rows to see the mojibake is baked into the bytes. Also: check WHEN affected rows were written (spanned Jan–Jul 2026, not a one-off) to decide legacy-vs-live; the batch worker skips non-empty content, so old bad rows persist until explicitly regenerated. [[dm_tools_backend_no_reload]]
- **No DB regen needed** — rows are already clean, and the CSV fix means future generations are clean (which also resolves the doubling at source, since dedup only failed because clean≠mojibaked forms differed). Deploy = kill+relaunch bare uvicorn (no `--reload`); `/api/version` → `bc68056` confirms.

## Nav apps-icon button — height-match, square→wider, purple, icon swaps (2026-07-18)

Follow-up polish on the "Dashboard → apps grid icon" nav button from 2026-07-17. Final state on `origin/main` (`2a42ee4`): icon-only button, **9-square grid** glyph, brand purple, **2.75rem wide × 2.25rem tall**. All CSS in `frontend/css/style.css` `.nav-dashboard-btn` / `.nav-dashboard-btn svg`; icon SVG is inline and hand-duplicated in every page's navbar.

- **Height-matching gotcha — don't fight it with padding math.** The button (`<a class="btn btn-light">`) rendered *taller* than the sibling `.nav-dropdown-toggle` menu buttons because Bootstrap's `.btn` forces `line-height:1.5` while the toggles are native `<button>`s at `line-height:normal`. Reducing the button's padding to compensate only got it *close* (residual ~1–4px, visibly off). **Deterministic fix: give BOTH `.nav-dropdown-toggle` and `.nav-dashboard-btn` an explicit `height` (2.25rem) + `box-sizing:border-box` + `display:inline-flex; align-items:center` and let the content centre.** Now height is independent of text-vs-icon content and they're pixel-identical. Setting `height` on the toggles is visually a no-op (≈ their natural height) but locks the match.
- **Keep the icon button OUT of the responsive `@media` padding/font rules.** Those rules (`.nav-dropdown-toggle, .nav-dashboard-btn { font-size…; padding… !important }`) re-add horizontal padding at <1600/1200/992px, which squeezes/overflows the fixed-size icon. Dropped `.nav-dashboard-btn` from all three media selectors so it stays a fixed box at every breakpoint (toggles still shrink their text; heights still match since `height` isn't overridden).
- **Purple icon = `fill="currentColor"` + `.nav-dashboard-btn svg { color:#5e4a90 }`.** The remote's icon shipped dark (inherited `btn-light` text colour); one CSS `color` rule on the svg recolours it because the glyph uses `currentColor`. (User's "still not purple" screenshot was a stale CSS cache — hard-refresh.)
- **"Square" then "slightly wider":** square = `width:2.25rem; height:2.25rem; padding:0`; slightly wider = bump `width` to `2.75rem`, keep height. Icon size is `1.55em` (em-based so it tracked the old responsive font-size).
- **Icon glyph swaps are a scripted per-file string replace across the 32 tracked pages** (9-square filled `<path>` ⇄ 2×2 rounded `<rect>`s, both `fill="currentColor"`). Tried a rounded-2×2 variant, user reverted to the 9-square grid.
- **Committing gotcha (recurring this whole nav thread):** every `frontend/*.html` also carries an *uncommitted* Healthscore-2.0 nav-link line from another session, and `frontend/healthscore.html` + `backend/healthscore_*` are untracked. To commit ONLY the nav change without disturbing Healthscore: script edits over **tracked** files only (`git ls-files 'frontend/*.html'`, skip healthscore.html), then stage **per-hunk** — `git diff -- 'frontend/*.html'` → keep only hunks whose `+` line contains your change's marker → `git apply --cached` (`style.css` is all-yours, plain `git add`). Verify `git diff --cached | grep -c healthscore` == 0 before commit. [[feedback_dm_dashboard_readonly]]
- **Drift with the other Claude:** mid-task, a `pull --rebase` hit conflicts on every button file — the remote (`70d330e` "match apps-icon nav button height to menu items") had *already* added an apps-icon button that diverged from my local approach (icon-only 9-square vs my icon+text). Reconciled by `rebase --abort` → `reset --hard origin/main` → `stash pop` the Healthscore WIP → rebuild the change on top of the remote version. Lesson: before a multi-file nav change, check whether the remote already touched it.

## GSD Campaigns — MC sub-accounts created without a store URL + latent service-account auto-detect bug (2026-07-20)

- **Symptom:** running Create GSD-campaigns created a new Merchant Center sub-account with an **empty "Uw online winkel" (online-store URL)**. `create_merchant_id` (in `gsd_campaigns_service.py`) built the account body with only `name`+`kind` and **never set `websiteUrl`** — whereas the original `create GSD-campaigns WB.py` DID (derived from the shop name). Beslist shop names ARE domains ("Hoopo.eu", "Calcuso.com|NL", "Ko-co.beauty"), so the URL is just `https://www.<shop_name>`.
- **Fix (code):** added `_shop_website_url(shop_name, country)` → `https://www.<cleaned-name>`, splitting off any `|`/` l ` suffix and lower-casing. **Keeps an existing TLD** (incl. `.eu`/`.beauty`) and only appends the country TLD when the name has NO TLD — the original blindly appended, which would turn "Hoopo.eu" into "hoopo.eu.nl". `create_merchant_id` gained an optional `website_url` and now always sets `body["websiteUrl"]`; `_get_or_create_mc_account` derives it (now takes `country`) and the run call-site passes `country`. **Affects NEW accounts only** — existing empty accounts are not backfilled by the run.
- **Backfill (done 2026-07-20):** scratchpad `mc_url_backfill.py` enumerated all sub-accounts under the 3 parent MCAs (NL `5592708765` / BE `5588879919` / DE `5342886105`), found **11 with empty websiteUrl (7 NL + 4 BE, DE 0)**, and set each via **get-then-update** (preserves `adsLinks` etc.). Verified 0 empty afterwards. Shops: Superfoodsonline, Calcuso.com|NL (pipe stripped → calcuso.com), Hoopo.eu (both NL+BE), Geurfris, Scentulp, Zurbrueggen, Gymbeam.
- **LATENT BUG found while backfilling:** `_get_mc_service()` picks the SA key by taking the **first `*.json` in `backend/service_accounts/`** when `GSD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE` is unset. Of the 4 keys there, **ONLY `acoustic-racer-258913-e55feb91bacc.json` has access** to the parent MCAs; the other 3 (`cla-campaign-creation`, `cla-test`, `seismic-machine`) return **HTTP 401 `auth/account_access_denied`**. `os.listdir` order is **not guaranteed**, so a deploy/restart on another box could silently pick a no-access key and fail every MC create/lookup. **Fix: set `GSD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE` explicitly to the acoustic-racer key in the deployed `.env`** (and/or make `_get_mc_service` prefer it by name). See TASKS. [[google_ads_python_credentials]]

## GSD Campaigns — LL pause/enable actually RUNS daily ~09:50 CEST via a hidden /ll/run trigger (2026-07-20)

Investigating a user report: "Enabled/Paused history shows entries from yesterday and the day before at exactly 09:50, but nobody triggered a run."

- **It is a real run, not just the data load.** Real pause/enable mutations land in `pa.jvs_gsd_ll_campaigns` **every day at 07:50:01–07:53 UTC (= 09:50 CEST)**, with second-level spread across many shops/campaigns (i.e. genuine per-campaign Google Ads mutations). Pattern **started 2026-07-17**; before that the last run was 2026-07-10 (~11:48 CEST, manual). It began the **morning after** the Windows task `DM-Dashboard-GSD-LL-Excel-Load` was created (`pa.scheduled_tasks` id=2, created 2026-07-16 13:46, DAILY 09:50).
- **The dm-tools code path CANNOT cause a mutation.** `/ll/excel-load` → `load_excel_data` → `fetch_feed_from_excel` only caches (pure Excel reader, zero side effects); the in-process `threading.Timer` scheduler (`_excel_scheduled_run`, `SCHEDULE_HOUR=9`/`SCHEDULE_MINUTE=50`) only loads; `run_low_linkage` is called **only** from `start_ll_run`, which is called **only** from `POST /ll/run` and `POST /ll/apply`. User confirmed: the Windows task runs **only** `curl -s -X POST .../ll/excel-load` (no `/ll/run`), and the **deployed `load_excel_data` is byte-identical** to the repo (no apply).
- **But the work IS done by the dm-tools backend itself** — ruling out an external direct-DB writer (e.g. n8n writing rows directly). Decisive test: `run_low_linkage` bumps `pa.jvs_gsd_ll_shop_cycles` **at the end** of a run via `_bump_shop_cycles`. Those `updated_at` timestamps bump at **07:53:02–04 on 07-20**, right after the campaign rows finish (07:53:02) — exactly the internal order of `run_low_linkage`. So something **POSTs `/ll/run?source=excel`** to the **same backend process** ~1s after the 09:50 excel-load (it reads the just-cached in-memory feed, hence `source=excel` and the tight 07:50:01 start).
- **Still unproven: WHERE the trigger lives.** Because it uses `source=excel` + the in-memory cache, it hits the backend process on l.davidowski's machine (`localhost:8003`). But whether the **caller** is local (`127.0.0.1`) or a **remote** host (LAN-exposed backend, e.g. an n8n workflow) is NOT decidable from the DB. My earlier "vrijwel zeker l.davidowski's machine" was **too strong** for the trigger location.
- **Decisive artifact now exists:** commit `6331838` "feat(gsd-ll): log IP and User-Agent on /ll/run calls" logs `ip / dry_run / source / user-agent` on every `/ll/run` (`gsd_campaigns_router.py:168-171`, needs `Request` param). Pulled into the local dm-tools checkout 2026-07-20. Once the **deployed** backend restarts onto this commit, tomorrow's 09:50 cycle will name the caller. See TASKS "GSD LL — confirm the 09:50 /ll/run trigger source". Lesson: a shared audit table can't tell you *who* wrote it — correlate a second table written by the same code path (here `shop_cycles`) to prove the code ran, then add request-level logging to find the caller.

## GSD Campaigns — LL last-load timestamp from file mtime, accordion detail rows, orange dry-run badge (2026-07-17)

Three follow-up tweaks (commits `90796f9` backend, `00a7935` frontend; dm-dashboard checkout).

But `backend/data/` isn't guaranteed to exist on the box → the write failed silently (caught), the read returned None → fell back to `now()`, so every server restart showed the restart time instead of ~09:50. **Fix: derive `loaded_at` from the Excel file's own mtime** (`datetime.fromtimestamp(os.path.getmtime(path), AMSTERDAM_TZ)`) — stable across restarts, reflects the real data date, and needs no writable state dir. Dropped the `_persist_load_time`/`_read_persisted_load_time` JSON dance. Lesson: don't persist a "when did X happen" timestamp to a maybe-missing dir when the source artifact already carries the time (file mtime).

## GSD Campaigns — change_event truncation missed labels + LL run-table Skipped count/header fixes (2026-07-17)

Follow-up on the bulk `GSD_LL_PAUSED` labeling below. Two things surfaced.

- **`change_event` `LIMIT 10000` over a busy account silently truncates → wrong pause dates.** The original labeling used ONE global `change_event` query per account (`DURING LAST_14_DAYS ... ORDER BY change_date_time DESC LIMIT 10000`) to date each campaign's pause. In the shared NL account (`7938980174`, hundreds of shops) 10k events don't even span a few days, so pauses from 13 juli fell outside the window and 10 campaigns were mis-dated as "before the 10-juli cutoff" and NOT labeled. **Fix pattern: query `change_event` PER CAMPAIGN** — `WHERE change_event.campaign='customers/{cid}/campaigns/{id}' AND change_event.change_date_time DURING LAST_14_DAYS ... LIMIT 100`. Few events per campaign → no truncation → reliable. A reliable full re-scan found exactly 10 missed (5 Geheugenhulp NL, 4 Houtenspeelgoed NL `label_test`, 1 Valhallaboardgames NL), all paused 13 juli; labeled them (verified). **Reliable "was it paused before the cutoff" signal without dates = absence of the `GSD_LL_PAUSED` label** (the LL tool only pauses since 10 juli and our task tagged every ≥10-juli pause). GAQL date literals: `LAST_14_DAYS`/`LAST_30_DAYS` exist but `LAST_29_DAYS` does NOT and `LAST_30_DAYS` errors `START_DATE_TOO_OLD` (must be <30d); use an explicit `>= 'YYYY-MM-DD'` range ~28d back instead.
- **LL run table (`renderPreviewPage`) undercounted Skipped groups to "1 campagne".** The run/preview table groups rows by `(shop_id, country)` and shows a count. Paused/Enabled entries are one row per campaign, but a **Skipped** entry is a single row per (shop, country) carrying a **nested `campaigns` array** (added by the "Dutch skip-reason labels" backend change), so `g.campaigns.length` counted it as 1 while the expand (`toggleLLPreviewDetail`) flattened the nested list. Fixed with `groupCampaignCount(group)` = `reduce` summing nested Skipped campaigns (mirroring the detail expansion), used for both the count label AND the Campaigns-column sort (`fix` commit `d19aba1`).
- **Styling:** gave the expandable detail sub-table (`.ll-detail-table th`) the same grey header (`#f8f9fa`) as `.ll-history-table th` (`46c0020`).
- **Working-copy note:** made both fixes in the **dm-dashboard** checkout, not dm-tools — dm-tools had another session's uncommitted **Healthscore** tool work (a nav-link line added to every `frontend/*.html` + untracked `healthscore.*`), so a pull/commit there would disturb it. Same remote → fix lands on `origin/main` regardless. [[feedback_dm_dashboard_readonly]]

## GSD Campaigns — ad-hoc bulk `GSD_LL_PAUSED` labeling of externally-paused campaigns (2026-07-17)

One-off ops task (no code committed; scripts live in session scratchpad `ll_label_*.py`). User gave `paused_ll_shops.xlsx` (33 rows, cols `Shopnaam` + `Country`, where Country can be `NL`, `BE`, `DE`, or `NL + BE`) and asked to add `GSD_LL_PAUSED` to paused campaigns whose name contains `[shop:{shopnaam}]`, in the listed countries, **only where the pause happened on/after 2026-07-10**. Applied to **101 campaigns, 0 errors** (verified all now carry the label; account-wide totals 234→335).

- **Match by name substring, not shop_id.** Campaign names carry BOTH `[shop:{shopnaam}]` and `[shop_id:{id}]`. Reuse `gsd_campaigns_service._name_contains_regexp(f"[shop:{shopnaam}]")` (REGEXP_MATCH, escapes `[` `]` `.`) — do NOT `LIKE '%[shop:X]%'` (brackets become a char-class and match ~everything). Country→account via `gsd_ll_service.COUNTRY_CUSTOMER_IDS`: NL = one acct `7938980174` (CPR+CPC share it), BE = TWO accts `2454295509`+`7565255758`, DE = `4192567576`.
- **Two independent sources of "when was it paused", and they answer different questions.** (1) LL audit log `pa.jvs_gsd_ll_campaigns` (`action='Paused'`, `created_at`, `campaign_id` is **text**) = when the *LL tool* paused it. (2) Google Ads `change_event` = when the campaign's status *actually* changed to PAUSED, regardless of who did it. Here the LL log held only tool-pauses (all since Jul 10, all already labeled) so it found **0** to do; the real 101 targets were paused **outside the tool** (bulk ops, e.g. many at exactly `2026-07-14 12:28:07`) and only `change_event` had their dates.
- **`change_event` GAQL gotchas (v24):** filter `change_event.change_resource_type = 'CAMPAIGN'` (NOT `resource_type`); mandatory `change_event.change_date_time DURING LAST_14_DAYS` (or `LAST_30_DAYS`) + `LIMIT`; you may NOT select nested subfields like `change_event.new_resource.campaign.status` — select the whole `change_event.new_resource` / `.old_resource` / `.changed_fields` and read `.campaign.status` off the returned proto in Python; check `'status' in changed_fields.paths`. `change_date_time` is `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS[.ffffff]` in the **account tz (Europe/Amsterdam)** — parse with optional `.%f`.
- **`GSD_LL_PAUSED` is a re-enable trigger, not just a tag.** The LL "Enable low linkage shops" pass finds label-carrying campaigns and RE-ENABLES them + strips the label ([[shop_campaign_178_bidding_blocker]] unrelated). So labeling externally-paused campaigns means a future enable-run turns them back ON. Flagged this; user chose to label **all 101** anyway (incl. **31** non-standard/test campaigns — `[label_test] …`, `[label:tag_toppers]`, `[label:merk]` — vs **70** standard `a/b/c/no_data/no_ean`). If they should stay paused, don't run the enable for those shops or strip the label.
- **Apply via** `_ensure_label(client, cid, "GSD_LL_PAUSED")` (creates per-account if missing; bg `#E0A800`) → `CampaignLabelService.mutate_campaign_labels` with `op.create.campaign = campaign_path(cid, id)`, `op.create.label = label_res`. Idempotency: pre-fetch the account's already-labeled set and skip (re-attaching an existing CampaignLabel errors). Creds/DB for a standalone script: `load_dotenv(dm-tools/.env)` then reuse `gsd_campaigns_service._get_client()` (env-based) + `psycopg2.connect(os.environ["DATABASE_URL"])`; run with `dm-tools/venv/bin/python`.

## GSD Campaigns — repair skipped an ad group whose tree was deleted (campaign-vs-ad-group scope bug) (2026-07-16)

Bug report: user removed the listing tree in campaign `[…][shop:Geurfris.nl][shop_id:666749][label:b]` (BE_CPR), but Create GSD-campaigns didn't repair it — yet removing the whole AD GROUP in the sibling `[label:no_data]` campaign WAS repaired. Fix in `backend/gsd_campaigns_service.py` (commit `b9aafe7`).

- **Root cause: `_repair_campaign`, `_tree_targets_label`, `_remove_listing_tree` and `_check_campaign_structure` queried listing-group / product-ad state at CAMPAIGN scope (`WHERE campaign.id = …`).** A campaign can carry a **REMOVED ad group whose child criteria/ads keep their OWN non-REMOVED status** (ad_group_criterion.status is independent of ad_group.status). Live diagnosis of that campaign: live AG `203588350772` (ENABLED) had only a single root `UNIT val=''` (the default Google auto-creates when you delete a product partition — the broken state), while REMOVED AG `206839893828` still had its full old tree (`SUBDIVISION` root PAUSED + `UNIT val='b'` ENABLED). The campaign-wide `has_lg`/`_tree_targets_label` read the dead AG's tree → "present and targets b, all good" → **skipped**. `[label:no_data]` worked only because removing the whole ad group left NO live ad group (`ags` empty → rebuild-everything path).
- **Fix: scope all four checks to the LIVE ad group (`WHERE ad_group.id = {ad_group_id}`).** `ad_group_id` = `ags[0]` resource tail. `_tree_targets_label`/`_remove_listing_tree` now take an ad_group_id (not campaign_id). `_check_campaign_structure` resolves the live AG first, returns `no_ad_group` early if none. No change for normal single-ad-group campaigns; strictly more correct. Verified live: fixed check reports the live AG's single-root-UNIT tree as wrong (`tree_ok=False` → retree), dead AG ignored.
- **General gotcha for Google Ads GAQL:** to assess an ad group's CURRENT structure, filter by `ad_group.id`, never `campaign.id` — removed sibling ad groups leave orphaned-but-still-ENABLED children that pollute campaign-level reads. `ad_group_criterion.status != 'REMOVED'` does NOT exclude criteria of a removed ad group.
- **Possible latent impact:** any GSD campaign that ever had an ad group removed+recreated could have been silently mis-assessed by the old code. Offered (not yet run) a full scan for live ad groups with missing/wrong trees. The Geurfris.nl `[label:b]` campaign itself is still broken until a repair re-run (offered).

## GSD Campaigns — creation-date column + per-(shop,country) date table (2026-07-16)

Added a "Date" (creation date only) column to Campaigns created, reordered its columns to match Enabled/Paused history (`Date | Shop | Country | Status | Campaign`; Status sits where history has Action) and switched it from `table-layout:fixed`+ellipsis to nowrap + horizontal scroll (same slider as the history table). Commits `6a06623` (feature), `c9aba8e`/`56d290e` (center Status + Action columns via `col-status`/`col-action` classes; also removed the low-linkage card-header "i" tooltip SVG).

- **No campaign creation-date exists in the Google Ads API.** `campaign.start_date` was removed in v24; the only real source is `change_event.change_date_time` where `resource_change_operation='CREATE'` — but **change_event retains only ~30 days**, and the API **rejects a start date exactly 30 days old** ("cannot be older than 30 days") so the query window must be **clamped to 29**. So dates can't be fetched live; they must be persisted.
- **New table `pa.jvs_gsd_campaign_created`** (n8n-vector-db Postgres), grain **(shop_id, country)** — PK `(shop_id, country)`, cols `created_date DATE, shop_name, recorded_at`. This is the natural grain: a shop's a/b/c label campaigns in a country are all created in one run, and the source spreadsheet is per-shop+country too. `get_all_gsd_stats` attaches `created_date` to each campaign via a single Postgres read joined on `_created_key(shop_id, country)` ("<shop_id>|<COUNTRY>", case-normalised); campaigns whose name doesn't parse a shop_id (rare, e.g. a name missing `[label:]`) stay `-`. Grows forward via `record_created_campaigns` at create time (best-effort, never fails a run). New endpoint `POST /api/gsd-campaigns/campaigns/backfill-created-dates` runs the change_event backfill.
- **`execute_values` + `cur.rowcount` LIES.** execute_values pages in batches of 100, so `cur.rowcount` reflects only the LAST page (reported "36" when all 736 rows inserted — 736 = 7×100 + 36). Use `... RETURNING 1` with `fetch=True` and `len(returned)` for an accurate insert count under ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.
- **Backfill got to 100% (2742/2743) via THREE sources**, layered (all ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING → first/earliest wins): (1) the user's spreadsheet `gsd_campaigns_creation_dates.xlsx` — 923 rows → 736 unique (shop_id,country), earliest kept (`scripts/backfill_gsd_creation_dates.py`); (2) change_event last-29-days → +14 recent shops; (3) Redshift eligibility + manual dates for the final 11.
- **Eligibility date ≠ creation date — and 2023-02-17 is a `bt.shop_list` flag-introduction artifact.** For blank shops we queried `MIN(date) WHERE is_gsd_{nl,be,de}_shop=1` in `bt.shop_list`. **Gotcha: on 2023-02-17, 792 shops got the flag in one bulk backfill** (2023-02-13..16 had only 2/day), so "eligible since 2023-02-17" means "flagged at intro", NOT real creation. Eligibility is only a good creation proxy for shops that flipped 0→1 **after the program launched (~2025-06-12, the spreadsheet's earliest, itself a bulk batch)**. Pre-launch shops' real dates were user-provided; Peterhahn.nl NL used its post-intro eligibility 2025-04-15.
- **Deploy gotcha: launching the backend with `nohup … &` inside the Bash tool does NOT persist** — the tool tears down the process group on return (survived once, died the next times). Use the Bash tool's `run_in_background:true` (with `exec uvicorn …`) for a persistent server. Backend is bare uvicorn (no --reload) → kill+relaunch to deploy; safe only when no run is active (`/run/progress`, `/ll/progress` both idle).

Created a durable blueprint so every new dm-tools page looks identical. Full spec lives in **`cc1/UI_BLUEPRINT.md`**; the copy-paste scaffold is **`frontend/_tool-template.html`** (commit `50240cb` on main). Frontend is static → live on refresh.

- **Design tokens are already in `frontend/css/style.css` `:root`** — don't hard-code hexes inline: `--color-navbar #5e4a90` (purple, navbar only), `--color-section #E8E9EB` (grey card headers), `--color-button #CC5500` (orange), `--color-button-hover #E97451` (coral).

- **Pagination orange arrows** = `btn btn-outline-secondary btn-page` — `btn-outline-secondary` maps to `--color-button` in style.css, which is *why* the chevrons are orange (this was the "orange arrows in Enabled/Paused history" the user meant). Use the chevron SVGs, not `<`/`>`.
- **Status bar:** hidden `#progressArea`; green (`#00b894`) striped/animated bar + label/percent line + **red-outline Cancel** below. Drive with `showStatus/setStatus/hideStatus`, honour `cancelRequested`.

- **Card headers = grey** (`.card-header` default). Decision call: **GSD Campaigns' inline purple (`#5e4a90`) headers are the outlier** — every other tool uses the style.css grey default, so the blueprint standardises on grey. Flip both template + doc if the user later prefers purple.
- **Footer (every page):** `<footer class="text-center py-4"><small class="text-muted">Digital Marketing tools by Joep van Schagen - 2026</small></footer>`.

## GSD Campaigns — why some Activity Log rows have no Reset button (2026-07-16)

`renderLog()` only renders a **Reset** button when an entry is a GSD create-run: either `entry.action === 'Run Script'` (reconstructs from Google Ads change history), or it carries a stored undo payload (`created`/`paused` > 0 → direct undo). **Everything else gets no Reset button by design** — individual/bulk Pause/Enable/Remove actions, LL runs, and Reset entries themselves. The Activity Log badge only distinguishes `LL` (action starts with `ll`) from everything-else (badge reads `GSD`), so a manual "1 activated (1 selected)" pause/activate row shows a GSD badge with no Reset — that's expected, not a bug. (This became moot for those actions after they stopped being logged; see entry above.)

Frontend-only polish on `frontend/gsd-campaigns.html` (commit `bf34bc5` → pushed `eb2841f` on main). Static file, live on browser refresh — no uvicorn restart.

- **Canonical dm-tools orange = `#CC5500`.** Counted the orange hexes across `frontend/*.html`: `#CC5500` ×61 (the standard), `#E97451` ×16 (its hover shade), `#E67E22` ×10, `#FD7E14` ×4. So the "correct" orange button is **`bg #CC5500`, hover `#E97451`** (filled, e.g. the Run button) or **outline `#CC5500`** (border+text, transparent bg, fill on hover). When asked to match "the other orange buttons", use `#CC5500` — don't invent a new shade.
- Aligned two stragglers on this page: the **Export history** button (`#fd7e14` → `#CC5500`, outline + hover-fill) and the **bulk Pause** button `.btn-bulk-pause` (`#e65100` → `#CC5500`, both the base rule and `:hover:not(:disabled)`). Activate (green `#00b894`) / Remove (red `#d63031`) left as-is — those aren't orange.
- **Button height:** the toolbar buttons (Refresh, Copy for Excel) are `btn btn-sm`; the Preview/Run pairs were full-size `btn` with `padding: 0.4rem …`. To match height, added `btn-sm` AND reduced the inline vertical padding to `0.25rem` — the **inline `padding` overrides `btn-sm`'s vertical padding**, so adding the class alone doesn't shrink height. Applied to BOTH pairs (Create section `previewScript`/`runScript`, Low-Linkage `runLowLinkage(true/false)`).
- **Equal width per pair:** "Preview" and "Run" differ in text length, so equal horizontal padding ≠ equal width. Fix = shared `padding` + a `min-width` so the shorter "Run" stretches to match. First tried `min-width: 120px` (too wide per user), settled on `padding: 0.25rem 1rem; min-width: 90px` on all four buttons.

## GSD Campaigns — LL per-shop pause/enable cycle tracking + repair REMOVED-tree fix (2026-07-16)

Follow-up on `backend/gsd_ll_service.py`, `backend/gsd_campaigns_router.py`, `backend/gsd_campaigns_service.py`, `frontend/gsd-campaigns.html` (commit `6f9b0fa` on main). Deploy = kill+relaunch bare uvicorn.

- **We already logged every LL pause/enable ACTION** (campaign-grained) in `pa.jvs_gsd_ll_campaigns` — but there was **no per-shop count** of how often a shop is paused vs re-enabled. Added a dedicated counter table **`pa.jvs_gsd_ll_shop_cycles`** (n8n-vector-db Postgres), grain **(shop_id, country)** — PK `(shop_id, country)`, cols `pause_count, enable_count, last_paused_at, last_enabled_at, currently_paused, updated_at`. User chose per-shop+country (not shop-only) so NL-vs-BE churn is distinguishable; roll up with `SUM … GROUP BY shop_name`.
- **Counting rule: one event per run per shop+country per action, NOT per campaign.** A run that pauses a shop's 5 campaigns must bump `pause_count` by 1. Implemented by collecting `cycle_events[(shop_id, country, action)] = shop_name` inside the mutation loop, then `_bump_shop_cycles` (INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE `+1`) once each after the loop — in BOTH `run_low_linkage` and `start_ll_apply`. Best-effort: a counter miss must never reclassify a real Ads mutation as an error (same discipline as `_record_action`).
- **Backfill `backfill_shop_cycles(gap_minutes=30, dry_run=True)`** — the action log has **no run_id**, so historical rows are grouped into events by time via a **gap-and-islands** SQL (LAG over `PARTITION BY shop_id, country, action ORDER BY created_at`; a gap > `gap_minutes` starts a new event). Bucketing by `date_trunc('minute')` would OVER-count a single multi-minute run — don't. Ran live: 277 campaign rows → **45 (shop,country) rows = 45 pause events, 0 enables** (Abckantoormeubelen correctly 1/country, not 3). `currently_paused` = last event was a pause.
- New endpoint `GET /api/gsd-campaigns/ll/shop-cycles`; `get_shop_cycles(limit)` reader.
- **Frontend:** Enabled/Paused history gets an **orange-outlined "Export history"** button (was `#fd7e14`, later aligned to the canonical `#CC5500` — see 2026-07-16 button-styling entry) → `exportLLShopCycles()` fetches the endpoint, aggregates per shop_name across countries in JS, exports `Shop / Times paused / Times re-enabled` (SheetJS, already loaded). Removed the redundant "Export Excel" there (deleted dead `exportLLXlsx`, kept `getLLRows` for Copy). **Campaigns-created "Copy for Excel"** now copies only CHECKED rows (`getSelectedCampaignRows` matches `.camp-check:checked` by `customer_id|campaign_id` against `filteredCampaigns`; alerts if none ticked).
- **`_repair_campaign` REMOVED-filter fix:** verified a manual test (removed the ad group in Zurbrueggen.nl BE `[label:c]`) — the repair DID recreate it (new ENABLED ad group + ad + 3-node tree; the deleted one lingers as REMOVED, which is why it *looked* un-repaired). The ad-group (`status != 'REMOVED'`) and product-ad checks already filtered REMOVED; the **listing-tree `has_lg` check did NOT** — the lone inconsistency. Added `AND ad_group_criterion.status != 'REMOVED'` so a removed-only tree no longer reads as present. In practice it was masked by the `_tree_targets_label` retree path (which filters REMOVED), but now the check means what it says.

## GSD Campaigns — MC-id Redshift logging, eventual-consistency retry root-cause, post-run verify (2026-07-16)

Session on dm-tools `backend/gsd_campaigns_service.py` (commit `56e65fa` on main). Started from "the standalone `create GSD-campaigns.py` pushes created merchant ids to Redshift at the end — do the same in the dm-tools tool," then diagnosed a real production defect (Hoopo.eu no_data campaign) and hardened against it.

- **MC-id logging to `pa.mc_ids_efficy`** (mirrors the original `push_to_redshift`). Table schema `(shop_name TEXT, shop_id BIGINT, mc_created BIGINT, domain TEXT, date VARCHAR)` — note **`domain` actually stores the COUNTRY** (NL/BE/DE), and `date` is `YYYYMMDD`. New `push_mc_ids_to_redshift(rows)` (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS + `execute_values`; best-effort, never fails the run). `_get_or_create_mc_account` now returns **`(mc_id, created)`** so only **genuinely new** MC sub-accounts are logged (existing/reused ones are skipped — matching the original's `mc_created` list, NOT every `mc_id`). Wired into `run_gsd_script` → `overall_results["mc_ids_pushed"]`. Uses the existing `_get_redshift_connection()` (env `REDSHIFT_*`), not the original's hardcoded creds.
- **Backfill for campaigns already created:** `backfill_recent_mc_ids_to_redshift(days=2, dry_run=True)`. **`campaign.start_date` was REMOVED in Google Ads API v24** (`UNRECOGNIZED_FIELD`) — so "created recently" comes from the **`change_event`** resource instead. change_event gotchas: needs a **finite** `change_date_time` range (both `>=` lower AND `<=` upper bound, else `CHANGE_DATE_RANGE_INFINITE`), a mandatory `LIMIT` (≤10000), only retains ~30 days; fields are `change_event.change_resource_type`/`resource_change_operation`/`campaign`. Deduped per `(shop_id, country, merchant_id)` so a shop's 2–5 label campaigns collapse to one row. Ran live `dry_run=False` → **12 MC ids pushed** (8 NL + 4 BE, 14/15 Jul); included Hema.nl's reused MC `702758524` — correct, because the ask was merchant ids of *campaigns created*, not *MC accounts created*.
- **Root-cause of the Hoopo.eu "no ad group" report** (via `change_event` timeline): the 14-Jul run DID create the no_data ad group (19:19:34), but the **product ad** failed transiently and only landed 37 min later (19:56, via a second run's `_repair_campaign`). So the ad group existed but was **empty** (no product ad, no listing tree) — reads as "no ad group" in the UI. A freshly-created ad group can reject a `ShoppingProductAd` with **`RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` until it propagates**; the old `_mutate_with_retry` (~15s budget) gave up. Note b's ad group also lagged 2m42s → there was API turbulence in that window.
- **Fix (root cause):** new `_is_parent_not_ready` (`RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` in the message) + `_create_child_with_retry(what, fn)` — mirrors `_create_campaign_with_retry` but for mutates that reference a **just-created ad group**: patient `_MERCHANT_LINK_RETRY_DELAYS` (5/10/20/30/60s ≈2min) on not-ready, short exponential backoff on transient. Safe to retry (mutates are atomic → nothing created on failure → no duplicates). Wired into `add_shopping_product_ad_group_ad`, `add_sub_cpr`, `add_sub_cpc` (all hit the same fresh ad group moments later).
- **Post-run verification:** `verify_run_campaigns(client, campaigns, recheck_delay=15)` + `_check_campaign_structure` return issues `no_ad_group`/`no_product_ad`/`no_listing_group`/`wrong_listing_tree` (reuses `_tree_targets_label`, so "verify says bad" == "a rerun's `_repair_campaign` would fix it"). Flagged campaigns are **re-checked once after a delay** to filter read-API propagation lag (avoid false alarms). Runs at end of `run_gsd_script` (new `verify: bool = True` kwarg, backward-compatible with the router's positional call) → `overall_results["verification"] = {checked, ok, problems:[…]}`. **Verification data is in the API response but the frontend does NOT display it yet** (`gsd-campaigns.html` unchanged). Tested live: all 5 current Hoopo campaigns OK; a bogus id correctly flags all three missing-structure issues.
- **Deploy:** bare uvicorn, no `--reload` → kill+relaunch to make this live. Ran everything from `dm-tools/venv` with `load_dotenv('.env')`.

## Healthscore 2.0 — HTML-sitemap URL selection redesign (Phases 1–5 done, 2026-07-15)

Redesign of "Healthscore", the twice-weekly job that populates per-category HTML sitemaps. Problem: only ~35% of monthly SEO visits landed on a set URL. New standalone module `dm-tools/backend/healthscore_service.py` (CLI `--action coverage|features|keywords|sitemap`), reads Redshift, **writes everything to the n8n Postgres** (`pa.*`) per user's explicit instruction (NOT Redshift). Runs on `dm-tools/venv/bin/python` (has google-ads + pandas + dotenv; `~/.mysql-venv` does NOT have google-ads/dotenv). Analysis scripts in `scripts/analysis/healthscore_*.py`; plan in `docs/HEALTHSCORE_2.0_PLAN.md`.

- **The real HS engine is `bt.hs_sitemap_input_details_deepestcat`** (3.3M rows, per-URL: avg_search_volume, opb_* revenue, avg/weighted_visits, and_count/and_shop_count/facet_count, `*_ok` quality gates, and selection mechanics `bakje`/`row_rank_bakje`/`sort`). **bakje/sort/*_ok are computed inside that table's build SQL.** `bt.new_hs_data` = denormalized output (datasets visits/new_urls/search_console). HS2.0 leaves the build SQL untouched — treats it as a read-only feature source and layers its own score+selection on top (shadow-comparable, non-invasive).
- **Data sources (user-corrected — do NOT use `bt.search_console` for any variable):** CTR & bounce come from the **SEO Stats source `datamart.fct_visits`** (seo_stats_service.py defs): CTR = `(number_of_bvb_clicks+number_of_outclicks)/visits` (clicks-PER-VISIT, CAN exceed 1, not a bounded rate), bounce = share of visits with `cpc_productclicks=0 AND ww_productclicks=0`. Revenue = `ww+cpc+affiliate_revenue` (omzet_visit). Per-URL grain via `dim_visit.url` (full URL incl domain + query; `new_hs_data.url` is path-only → normalize BOTH sides: strip scheme/host, strip `?`/`#`, lowercase, rtrim `/`). SEO channel = `chan_deriv.ref_channel_derivation_stats.marketing_channel='SEO'`, `is_real_visit=1`. Filter host `^https?://www\.beslist\.nl/`. Coverage denom = fct_visits organic, NOT `search_console.visits`.
- **Phase 1 diagnosis — the 35% is ENTIRELY an R-url problem.** Overall coverage 41–45% (Apr–Jun). Non-R-url coverage ≈86% (C-url ~90%, PLP ~78–80%, Browse ~100%); **R-url ~3–5% and R-urls are ~51% of SEO visits.** The old set held only ~16k R-urls (of ~5.5M) — R-urls (product-refine/search pages) were structurally excluded by the `*_ok` gates. `pa.healthscore_coverage` logs per-type_url + `__ALL__` coverage per run.
- **`bt.hs_r_urls` = candidate universe ONLY** (~5.5M url + deepest_subcat_id, NO signals) → HS2.0 builds R-url features itself from the same fct_visits join (R-url = `type_url='R-url'`, no special case).
- **Phase 3 backtest — the model is far simpler than expected.** Predictor = features as-of end-of-month M (90d level window + 14d momentum), holdout = complete month M+1 (no leakage). Coordinate-ascent weights maximizing `0.5·visit_cov + 0.5·rev_cov` **collapsed to `f_visits 0.889 · f_rev 0.111`, with CTR/bounce/momentum/search-volume all = 0.000**, and reproduced EXACTLY across two splits (Apr→May and May→June). Reason: recent visits autocorrelate with future visits, and coverage only asks "was a visited URL selected?" — so trailing visits dominate; the other named variables move *value/quality*, not raw coverage. **The win mechanism is (1) include R-urls in the candidate universe + (2) per-category top-N cap — NOT a clever multi-variable score.** Keep CTR/bounce only as optional junk-filter guardrails.
- **Search volume earns ZERO weight (tested, negative).** Built the Keyword Planner cache anyway (`--action keywords`, `pa.hs_keyword_search_volume`, 327k R-url r_terms, 38.6% with volume, ran on a SINGLE customer id / 32 batches → **API limits are a non-issue**: 10k keywords/request, 35 rotating ids, ~monthly refresh, cache read by twice-weekly runs = 0 added calls). Adding f_vol as a 6th feature → weight 0.000, coverage unchanged. For URLs with visit history, realized visits beat keyword estimates; cold-start terms weren't fetched and are junk-contaminated anyway. **CAVEAT: raw r_term volume is dominated by navigational/brand junk** (weer 7.5M, google/marktplaats/telegraaf/albert heijn 5M — zero commercial intent). Cache is parked/unused by the scored model.
- **Phase 4 selection + writer** (`--action sitemap --cap-n 1000`): score computed server-side in Postgres (`percent_rank()` window fns on `pa.hs2_features`), top-N per `deepest_category_id`, + guaranteed **new-URL bucket** = user's Redshift query on `bt.facet_facetvalues` (facet values with min&max `load_start_date` within 20d = genuinely new; use the `url` column NOT `facet_url` which is just the token; country nl). Writes `pa.hs2_sitemap` (PK as_of,npath; source scored|new).
